data_as_of.statement: as of 2026-11-24, total 868 events in DB (675 non-MS)
data_as_of.note: The DB is refreshed every few months. Counts reflect the DB contents as of the latest event timestamp above. MCP reads the same events.db as the Postmortem web app, so no separate web pull is needed; both reflect the same snapshot.

query_defaults.hide_ms_meaning: Exclude Machine Study (*MS) periods from event lists/counts. MS is not a user beam-service period.
query_defaults.fault_classification: COALESCE(user_fault_type, fault_type): the manual user case designation overrides the automatic classifier.
query_defaults.interlock_fault_rule: The RF interlock fault is the first digital interlock in the trip chain (time_groups FIRST), not the most frequent channel.

abbreviations.note: Read this before interpreting device names. It defines the facility/SRF/protection terms, channel prefixes, instrument tags, and numeric suffixes used in events, alarms, and notes.

entries.note: 처음 연결한 에이전트가 장치명/PV를 추측하지 않도록 정리한 약어표다. 표에 없는 약어는 DB의 description, alarm catalog, notes를 확인하고 추측하지 않는다.

PLS-II.meaning_ko: 3 GeV 저장링 방사광 가속기. 이 데이터의 머신.

PLS.meaning_ko: 2.5 GeV 전신기. PLS-II와 다른 머신이므로 수치를 혼용하지 않는다.

SRF.meaning_ko: 초전도 고주파 시스템. CM 3기와 LLRF/HPRF로 구성.

CM.meaning_ko: 초전도 캐비티가 들어 있는 냉동모듈. CM1~CM3.

LLRF.meaning_ko: 캐비티 gap voltage의 amplitude와 phase를 closed loop로 제어하는 저전력 RF 계통.

HPRF.meaning_ko: LLRF 신호를 500 MHz 고출력으로 증폭하는 계통. KSU/KLY 포함.

KSU.meaning_ko: HPRF의 klystron 전원/보호 유닛. KSU1~KSU3. DC24V SMPS, HVPS, ion pump, cooling, focus 등을 포함한다.

KLY.meaning_ko: 500 MHz 고출력 RF를 만드는 진공관 증폭기.

IC.meaning_ko: MIS/PSI 외부 인터록을 각 LLRF와 KSU로 분배하는 장치.

FC.meaning_ko: LLRF의 field 제어 채널. 채널명의 FC#는 LLRF 채널 번호.

RF station.meaning_ko: CM 1기당 한 쌍으로 구성되는 독립 RF 계통.

CG.meaning_ko: 액체헬륨/밸브박스 냉동 계통. CG fault는 BPR01 압력 인터록으로 이어질 수 있다.

MIS.meaning_ko: 진공/빔튜브·빔라인 온도/방사선량/게이트밸브를 감시. 트립 시 RF Ready를 끊어 RF를 OFF.

PSI.meaning_ko: 출입/인명/방사선 안전 인터록. MIS와 별개이며 PSI trip도 RF Ready를 끊을 수 있다.

MPS.meaning_ko: 대용량 마그넷 전원 보호 계통. 마그넷 전원을 끊어 빔 손실을 만들며 RF를 직접 끄지 않는다.

BLM.meaning_ko: 빔손실 모니터링 계측기. 그 자체가 빔을 덤프하지 않는다.

OPI.meaning_ko: EPICS 운전 화면. 'MIS OPI'는 MIS 운전 화면/로그.

instrument_tags.BCL01/BCL03: CM 캐비티 bottom/top equator 온도 센서(CLTS-2B). BCL03은 quench-unit 온도로도 인용.
instrument_tags.BPR05: 밸브박스 cold gas return 압력 트랜스듀서.
instrument_tags.BPS01: CM helium vessel 압력 스위치(dry contact).
instrument_tags.BPS02: He warm return 압력 스위치(dry contact).

suffix._v: 정규화된 아날로그 채널. 정상 1.0, 물리 단위 아님.
suffix._d: 디지털 인터록 채널. 극성은 채널별 active_low/active_high.

examples: VAC_CM1_FC1_d = CM1 진공 인터록, FC1(LLRF) 채널, digital.
INT_MIS1_IC_d = MIS 이중화 1, Interlock Controller digital.
SR:RF:CRM1:BCL03 = 저장링 RF CM1의 cavity top equator 온도 센서.

topics.beam_energy_loss_after_rf_trip: RF trip 이후 빔 에너지 손실

physics_glossary.usage: Call postmortem_get_glossary(topic=<key>) for equations, citations, and caveats. topic='list' returns the full index.

analysis_contract.title: MCP event-analysis contract
evidence_order: 2. first digital interlock and quench_unit / quench_units_with_quen_assert
3. per-cavity sequence (90/50/10% times), not a class-level median
4. reliability flags: tau_reliable, cavity_tau_span_us, per-cavity tau
5. image panel mapping: images[].scope and visible_channels
6. root cause stated in notes, then cause_candidates as hypotheses
rules: physics.class is an observational pattern, never a root-cause label.
If tau_reliable=false, do not quote a single decay tau; report the 90-10% span and two-stage/slow tail.
A cavity probe dip followed by a rise is beam-loading/phase-slip oscillation, not 'recovery'.
RDY_KSU# can be downstream of QUEN_CM#, ARC_CM#, VAC_CM#, or a beam-loss event; check the earliest digital.
Do not call multi-cavity collapse simultaneous unless the per-cavity 50/10% times agree.
Forward power around 1.1-1.2 is the post-limit value from over-input protection (~1.2x), not the LLRF demand.
Do not invent He-cooling loss, thermal runaway, or QL collapse unless the note or logs state it.
For a CM single-fault example, prefer CM ARC or CM flowmeter/water-flow events; quench events often mix in multi-cavity/propagation effects.
tool_sequence: postmortem_search_notes(query) only for similar operator wording, not for counts

good_examples.why: CM3 ARC only; single cavity collapse; first digital ARC_CM3; clean CM single-fault example.
KSU3 HVPS water flow low; CM3 station RF off; one cavity collapses; clean flowmeter/station example.

bad_examples.why: CM1 quench, but class=rf_trip and 3 cavities eventually collapse; tau_reliable=false. Do not use as the canonical single-CM example, do not quote tau=17 ms, and do not call the collapses simultaneous.

tool_descriptions.postmortem_get_capabilities: Return live data coverage counts (events, notes, attachments, alarms, PV selections, PV catalog), the data_as_of snapshot date and total, index freshness, available tools, examples, and known limitations. Call this first. It also returns abbreviations: the device-name table for CM, LLRF, HPRF, KSU, IC, MIS, PSI, MPS, BLM, BPM, DCCT, TFS, FOFB, BCL01/BCL03, BPR01, BPS01, and channel prefixes. Read it before interpreting device tags. The DB is refreshed every few months, so quote the data_as_of date whenever you report totals.
tool_descriptions.postmortem_search_events: Search beam-dump events by natural-language query and/or structured filters. Filters: year, year_from/year_to, year_min/year_max, date (YYYY-MM-DD), subsystem (KSU1-3/CM1-3/CRG/MPS...), fault_type (string or list), fault_types (list), event_id, pv (matches event_alarms/event_pv_selection PV names), beam_time (partial beam-time label such as '2026-11차'), has_waveform (bool), hide_ms (default true; excludes Machine Study beam times such as 2026-01MS), sort ('relevance'|'recent'), limit, offset. fault_type/fault_types match the manual user_fault_type first, then the automatic fault_type. Questions containing 최근/요즘/최신 automatically use sort='recent'. Returns response_type='event_list' with items[]; each item has id, event_id, timestamp, fault_type (auto), auto_fault_type, effective_fault_type (manual override first), case_id (auto), effective_case_id (manual override first), classification_note (set only when manual differs from auto), user_fault_type, notes, alarm_count, pv_selection_count, has_waveform, url, citation. Use aggregate for counts.
tool_descriptions.postmortem_get_event: Return one event's full context: notes, fault classification (effective_fault_type applies the manual override first), recorded alarms, manual PV selections, catalog mappings, attachments, similar events, waveform availability. Returns response_type='event_detail' with event, alarms[], pv_selection[], catalog[], attachments[], similar[], waveform, caveats. An empty similar[] means the DB has no event_links for this event, not an API error. Set include_images=true (or waveform_image=true) to append MCP Image blocks for the pre-rendered forward/cavity/reflect JPEGs; image_scope=all|forward|cavity|reflect or a comma list. JSON stays in content[0].text. image records include event_id, visible_channels, and panel caption.
tool_descriptions.postmortem_explain_event: Preferred single-event explanation tool. Returns a deterministic evidence bundle: event, manual-vs-auto classification, primary_interlock, quench unit/source, per-cavity sequence, tau_reliable, per-cavity tau, root_cause from notes, mechanism steps, warnings, claim_checks, required_disclosures, and image panel metadata. Use this before writing any causal explanation. The physics.class is explicitly marked observational; do not use it as a root-cause label. Set include_images=true to append MCP Image blocks.
tool_descriptions.postmortem_analyze_cohort: Summarize a cohort of waveform events by class, quench_unit, first interlock, fault_family, year range, tau_reliable, beam delay range, or waveform availability. Returns counts/distributions, median/min/max beam delay, and representative examples sorted by delay. Use this for whole-dataset patterns; then call postmortem_explain_event for examples. Do not use vector search for counts.
tool_descriptions.postmortem_find_examples: Return curated teaching examples by topic. Topics include cm_single_fault (CM ARC/flowmeter, not quench), ksu_single_station, and quench_propagation (with explicit cautions). Each example includes why_clean, caution, summary, warnings, and waveform image metadata. Use this before choosing an event as a canonical example.
tool_descriptions.postmortem_search_notes: Hybrid lexical + dense retrieval over operator event notes. Use it to find similar wording/cases, not for counts, timing, or causal proof. Returns event_id, timestamp, fault_type, notes, dense/lexical scores, citation, and url. Falls back to lexical search if onnxruntime/model files are unavailable.
tool_descriptions.postmortem_route_question: Rule-based routing hint for a natural-language question. Returns recommended tools, glossary topics, suggested filters, cautions, and a reminder that the route is not an answer. Use it when unsure which MCP tools to call first.
tool_descriptions.postmortem_aggregate_events: Count events grouped by one or more fields. group_by accepts year, month (YYYY-MM), fault_type, case_id, auto_case_id, auto_fault_type, user_fault_type, beam_time, or a comma-separated composite such as 'year,beam_time'. case_id follows the manual classification first; auto_case_id is the automatic reference. fault_type grouping uses the manual user_fault_type first, then the automatic fault_type. Filters: year, year_from, year_to, subsystem, fault_type (string or list), fault_types (list), text, pv, beam_time. hide_ms (default true) excludes Machine Study periods. include_percent defaults to true. Rows carry key, count, percent; copy them verbatim and never estimate or recompute. Returns response_type='aggregate' with group_by[], total, sum_of_counts, rows:[{key, keys, count, percent?}], and data_as_of (latest event timestamp, DB total, and an 'as of YYYY-MM-DD, total N events' statement). Quote the data_as_of date when reporting totals. Use this for counts/trends; do not use vector search for counts.
tool_descriptions.postmortem_similar_events: Return events linked to the given event by the DB event_links similarity graph. Returns response_type='event_list' with event_id, returned, items[]; each item has both id and event_id. Empty items means no links exist in the DB. This is not a vector similarity score.
tool_descriptions.postmortem_search_alarm_catalog: Search the 524-entry alarm PV catalog by PV name, description, or graph PV. Returns response_type='pv_list' with items[]; each item has pv, description, subsystem, graph_pv, graph_description, severity, citation. Results are catalog mappings, not evidence that an alarm occurred in an event.
tool_descriptions.postmortem_get_alarm_status: Return the live alarm monitor status, last-state counts, and recent transitions. Returns response_type='alarm_status' with monitor, last_state_counts, last_state_updated, recent_transitions, catalog, caveats. Check last_heartbeat and last_state_updated before calling this current.
tool_descriptions.postmortem_resolve_event: Resolve a date (YYYY-MM-DD) and optional subsystem to candidate event IDs. Returns response_type='event_list' with returned and items[] (id + event_id). If multiple events match, choose one and call postmortem_get_event.
tool_descriptions.postmortem_list_fault_types: List fault types with descriptions, severity, and event counts. Counts use the manual user_fault_type first, then the automatic fault_type. hide_ms (default true) excludes Machine Study beam times. Returns response_type='fault_type_list' with items[].
tool_descriptions.postmortem_list_beam_times: List user beam-time labels with event counts. hide_ms (default true) omits Machine Study (*MS) beam times. Returns response_type='beam_time_list' with items[].
tool_descriptions.postmortem_get_pv_series: Return an Archiver time-series summary for a PV around an event's t0. Parameters: event_id, pv, pre=60, post=10, include_points=false. Supports KSU/CRM/CRG/LRF/G00 PVs. Returns response_type='pv_series' with available, quality, summary:{count,min,max,median,peak_value,peak_rel_sec,max_deviation_pct,resolution_s}, and optional points[].
tool_descriptions.postmortem_analyze_waveform: Return numeric waveform features for one event from the static feature store: t0, beam-current fall timing, CM1/2/3 cavity sag, reflect rise, forward trip, digital interlock transitions, quench unit, and data caveats. The 'sequence' block adds cavity 90/50/10% crossing times, the cavity-to-beam delay, the 3-cavity collapse spread, and a sequence pattern (rf_trip, beam_first_rf_trip, beam_only, single_cavity_quench, mixed). The pattern is descriptive; root cause is not assigned. The 'physics' block adds a deterministic textbook-grounded interpretation with PLS-II parameter checks, citations, cause_candidates (possible causes, not a root-cause assignment), and next_logs_ko. A cavity probe dip-and-rise is an oscillation, not necessarily 'recovery'. Covers 313/866 events (2023+, parquet only). Values are computed by code, not an LLM. Returns response_type='waveform_analysis'. Set generate_plot=true (or include_images=true) to append MCP Image blocks for the pre-rendered narrow-scope JPEGs; image_scope=all|forward|cavity|reflect. JSON stays in content[0].text. Use postmortem_find_similar_waveforms to compare waveforms; use postmortem_get_event for notes/alarms.
tool_descriptions.postmortem_find_similar_waveforms: Return the top_k events whose waveform feature vector is closest (cosine) to the given event. Model waveform_manual_v1 is a 78-dim hand-crafted vector (sag/reflect/forward/beam-fall/digital), not a learned embedding. Returns response_type='waveform_similarity' with target and items[] (event_id, similarity, signature, delta_vs_target, citation). Only events with parquet are searchable. This is not the DB event_links graph.
tool_descriptions.postmortem_search_reports: Search the indexed maintenance/fault reports (91 unique HWP/HWPX/PDF/DOCX documents from 96 attachments) by text and image captions. Hybrid FTS5 trigram + dense cosine (multilingual-e5-small, CPU only), reciprocal-rank fused. Parameters: query, event_id (optional), top_k (<=30). Returns response_type='report_search' with items[]: kind='chunk' (table/narrative text) or kind='image' (Qwen2.5-VL caption + OCR), title, event_id/event_ids, text/caption/ocr_text, citation [R:event/doc] or [R:event/doc#imgN], dense_score, fts_score. Treat VLM-transcribed numbers as pointers to the source image, not ground truth. Use postmortem_get_event for notes/alarms and postmortem_search_events for event lists.
tool_descriptions.postmortem_analyze_quench: Integrated quench analysis for one event: 100 ms waveform features (cavity sag, reflect rise, forward trip, beam fall, QUEN asserts), Archiver BCL01/BCL03 cavity temperatures and beam current around the Archiver t0, and report text/image-caption evidence. Parameters: event_id, include_pv=true, include_reports=true, include_images=false, image_scope=all|forward|cavity|reflect, pre=60, post=120. Returns response_type='quench_analysis' with event, waveform, pv.series, reports.items, highlights, caveats. PVs are ~1 Hz; waveform t0 and Archiver t0 are different clocks.
tool_descriptions.postmortem_compare_quench_events: Compare waveform features across up to 20 quench events. Parameters: event_ids (list), include_reports=false. Returns response_type='quench_comparison' with rows[]: timestamp, quench unit, t0, cavity sag/pre-state, reflect rise, forward trip, beam fall, QUEN assert, report titles. Use postmortem_analyze_quench for PV/temperature evidence; this table is fast and does not call the Archiver.
tool_descriptions.postmortem_get_glossary: Return curated background knowledge for PLS-II SRF beam-dump postmortems. This is a static, textbook-grounded reference library, not event data. Call it before interpreting waveform features, writing a causal chain, or answering any SRF/beam-physics question. DOMAIN GLOSSARY (config/domain_glossary.json), 10 addressable topics: abbreviations (device names and channel prefixes: CM, LLRF, HPRF, KSU, IC, MIS, PSI, MPS, BLM, BPM, DCCT, TFS, FOFB, BCL01/BCL03, BPR01, BPS01; read this before expanding a device tag), system_overview (ring/RF layout and operating context), interlock_hierarchy (external MIS/PSI vs internal CM/KSU trip chain), trip_sequence (standard MIS beam-dump sequence, first-interlock rule), signals (analog/digital definitions, active_low/active_high polarity), naming (actual PV/channel names), data_rules (MS exclusion, manual vs auto classification, relay delay), answer_style (required caveats and quoting rules), authority (document/data authority order), caveats (standing limitations). PHYSICS LIBRARY (config/physics_references.json), 8 topics and 31 references: cavity_figures_of_merit (Q0, QL, R/Q, beta, U, Pc, Pbeam, beta_opt), cavity_decay_after_rf_off (tau=2QL/omega; PLS-II 95-108 us natural, 24-32 us beam-loaded, midpoint 28 us), beam_loading_llrf (V_c=V_g+V_b; beam phase slip/beam loading can make the probe voltage oscillate; over-input protection limits forward to about 1.2x nominal; He vessel/rupture disk protection), mis_machine_interlock (PLC 3-layer MIS; RF Ready = MIS healthy AND PSI healthy; PSI handles radiation/access; MPS is separate; BLM is monitoring), beam_energy_loss_after_rf_trip (dE/dt=-U0/T_rev=1.32 GeV/ms; PLS-II RF acceptance 2.8% at 4.5 MV), transverse_instability (exponential growth; PLS-II TFS and FOFB; BPM limits), beam_dump_causes (empirical PLS-II taxonomy: RF single station, RF common, MPS, MIS, CONTROL/TFS/FOFB, BEAMLINE, MECHVAC, KICKER, MAGNET, PSI, LINAC, external; each class also lists cause_candidates), pls2_operating_point (3 GeV, 400 mA, 499.973 MHz, 3 cavities at 1.5 MV each = 4.5 MV, Q0/Qext, R/Q=89 ohm, RF acceptance 2.8%). The full physics document also carries one internal test note (2020-04-05 vertical test, 500 MHz CESR-B): it is measured test data, not a textbook citation, and is under 'internal_test_notes'. A physics topic returns title, summary_ko, equations[{name,expr,note}], categories[] (for beam_dump_causes), citations[{id,title,authors,year,doi,url,locator,supports}], and caveats. A domain topic returns its JSON object or entry list. Parameters: topic (optional). topic='list' returns the topic index only. Omit topic to return both documents (physics under 'physics'). An unknown topic returns the valid keys. Quote equations and parameter values from the response; do not substitute values from memory.

arguments.query: 켄치 발생 시 RF 반사파가 증가한 원인

event_list.items: array of event refs; each has id and event_id

pv_list.items: array of {pv, description, subsystem, graph_pv, citation}

report_search.items: array of {kind: chunk|image, title, event_id, event_ids, text|caption, score, dense_score, fts_score, citation}

session.note: Re-initialize the MCP session after expiry.

limitations: Report text and image captions/OCR cover parsed report attachments; VLM-transcribed numbers should be checked against the source image. Call postmortem_get_capabilities for current document counts.
report_md is auto-generated boilerplate and is not used as knowledge.
event_alarms snapshots exist for only a few events; most events have none.
event_pv_selection is a manually registered PV list, not a recorded alarm.
Waveform numeric features cover events with parquet (2023+); a few events have missing channels. Events without parquet cannot be analyzed. Call postmortem_get_capabilities for current coverage.

Event lists/counts exclude Machine Study (*MS) periods by default (hide_ms=true). MS is not a user beam-service period, so it is not data. Fault counts prefer the manual user_fault_type over the automatic fault_type.
Analog waveform values are normalized so nominal operation is 1.0; they are not physical units. Call postmortem_get_glossary or read postmortem://domain-guide before interpreting waveform features.
The RF interlock fault is the first digital interlock in the trip chain (time_groups FIRST), not the most frequent channel. MIS is dual-redundant (INT_MIS1_IC / INT_MIS2_IC).

A cavity probe voltage that dips and then rises is not necessarily 'recovering'; it can oscillate because of beam phase slip and beam loading. PLS-II over-input protection limits forward power to about 1.2x nominal.
physics.class is an observational pattern, not a root cause. Use postmortem_explain_event for primary_interlock, quench_unit, tau_reliable, warnings, and claim_checks.
If tau_reliable=false (90-10% span is long/two-stage), do not quote a single decay tau. Report the span and per-cavity values instead.
RDY_KSU# can be downstream of QUEN_CM#, ARC_CM#, VAC_CM#, or beam loss. Check the earliest digital before naming a root cause.
